outline.description: This chapter provides the technical and procedural foundation of the case, explaining the nature of the patents at issue and the legal standards the Federal Circuit used to review the district court's decisions.
subtopics: Technical background: Intermodulation Products (IMP) and Passive Intermodulation (PIM)
Procedural posture: From jury verdict to JMOL and appeal
Standard of review for denial of Judgment as a Matter of Law (JMOL) under Fifth Circuit law
The 'substantial evidence' standard for reviewing factual findings of infringement

outline.description: This chapter examines the court's reasoning for reversing the infringement verdict for the '134 patent, focusing on the failure of the plaintiff's expert to prove that the accused devices sampled the required signals.
subtopics: Analysis of Limitation 1[a]: Over-sampling 'signals of interest' and 'interference generating signals'
Dr. Wells' mapping of the 'modeled PIM path' to the claim terms
The logical impossibility of sampling signals generated downstream of the ADC
Evaluation of the expert's 'pivot' to x1 and x2 signals
The legal consequence of self-contradictory expert testimony in satisfying the burden of proof

outline.description: This chapter explores the legal and factual distinctions between the number of unique input signals and the number of required mathematical operations in the '775 patent.
subtopics: Claim construction: 'Three signals S1, S2 and S3' as 'separately identifiable' vs. 'unique'
Prosecution history: The impact of the Filipovic prior art on claim scope
Analysis of Limitation 1[d]: The requirement for seven specific third-order multiplications
Comparison between the Nokia technical document and the claimed multiplications
Failure of the expert to map three distinct multiplications to the seven claimed operations

outline.description: The final chapter explains the court's ultimate ruling and the automatic effect that the non-infringement findings had on the monetary award.
subtopics: Reversal of the district court's denial of JMOL for both patents
The relationship between the infringement finding and the damages award
Vacating the $166 million lump-sum damages award
